 Live .  3,713 viewing 3713 viewing Live page Updated 16 minutes ago Nvidia launches investigation into CEO's affair with suspected Chinese spy
 Summary
 US tech giant Nvidia opens an independent investigation following reports its CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with a suspected Chinese spy
 The company, one of the most valuable in the world, says its board has no reason to believe Nvidia's secrets or national security were compromised
 US intelligence officials believe Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who had a close relationship with Huang, was a spy for Beijing, according to the New York Times
 Huang admits to having been "unfaithful" to his wife and apologises for hurting her and their children
 Nvidia, which is seen as central to making the hardware for emerging AI technologies, says Huang is committed to continuing to lead the company
 The tech world has been stunned by the news, which could have enormous consequences, writes our tech and AI editor Zoe Kleinman 
 Live Reporting
 Edited by Gavin Butler with reporting from Zoe Kleinman and Fan Wang
 What we know about Megaspeed published at 04:10 GMT 04:10 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Megaspeed is a data centre company based in Singapore that buys Nvidia chips.
 US authorities had investigated Megaspeed last year for allegedly helping Chinese firms bypass trade restrictions to access Nvidia chips.
 Megaspeed has again found itself in the spotlight after Nvidia announced it was investigating CEO Jensen Huang for allegedly having a relationship with a Chinese spy.
 The New York Times has identified the Chinese spy as Alice Huang, a former executive of Megaspeed.
 Megaspeed, in a statement to The New York Times, said that “current leadership” takes the matter “extremely seriously and is committed to getting to the facts behind these allegations”.
 It said it has commissioned an internal investigation to be done by outside counsel.
 Megaspeed has bought $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips in the last two years, according to reports, making it one of Nvidia's biggest customers in South East Asia.

 Some Chinese social media users think this is just an affair published at 03:40 GMT 03:40 GMT 
 Fan Wang 
Live page reporter 
 Chinese social media users woke up to a shock this morning when they saw reports that Jensen Huang had admitted to having an affair.
 Hashtag "Jensen Huang admits affair" has generated nearly 10 million views within just hours, while "The person Jensen Huang cheated with" and several other hashtags are also gaining traction.
 But as is often the case in tightly controlled China, there are already signs of censorship and, in some cases, self censorship. 
 Although these topics are generating more engagement than most other hashtags, they remain relatively low on the trending chart.
 Chinese media is unsurprisingly muted on the spy allegation. Those outlets that did report on Huang's statement omitted mention of national security concerns, as well as accusations that Alice Huang is a Chinese spy.
 Many social media users appear to think this is no more than a marital scandal. "He wants to ge a divorce and protect some of his assets," one Weibo user wrote. 
 "He just made a mistake every man could have made," wrote another, referencing a phrase used by movie star Jackie Chan when referencing his own extramarital affair in 1999.
 Some "self-media" accounts, which are not affiliated with state media, were not oblivious to the espionage allegation, though they stopped short of discussing it in details. 
 "Is she a Chinese spy or American spy?" one user asked. "It's just political maneuvering," another user wrote.

 What is Nvidia? published at 03:15 GMT 03:15 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images US tech giant Nvidia is the world's most valuable publicly-traded company - worth some $4.5tn (£3.4tn) - and a leading provider of advanced computer chips.
 AI relies on large banks of servers, run on chips like these, to operate.
 Nvidia provides this technology to major firms such as OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT, and Meta, and has grown amid the AI boom.
 Its chips have been a major focus of the rivalry between the US and China, who are locked in an AI race - with America having long been concerned about Beijing's access to advanced computing technology.
 Washington has restricted exports of the most advanced Nvidia chips to Beijing since 2022, citing national security concerns and the risk that they could strengthen China's military operations - although there has been some loosening of restrictions under President Trump.

 China rejected spy report as baseless 'smear' published at 02:40 GMT 02:40 GMT 
 China has previously rejected allegations of a Chinese espionage operation targeting Jensen Huang.
 After the NYT reported the claims last month, Chinese foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said: "The report in question is based on groundless speculation and is nothing more than an attempt to smear China."

 Who is the suspected spy at the centre of Nvidia's investigation? published at 02:26 GMT 02:26 GMT 
 The New York Times (NYT) reported last month that US intelligence officials believe Alice Huang, who had a close relationship with the Nvidia boss, was a spy for Beijing.
 The paper reported that American intelligence agencies had been monitoring the Chinese businesswoman - who is of no relation to Jensen Huang - and concluded that she was acting on behalf of Beijing, citing unnamed sources.
 Surveillance reportedly revealed communications between the suspected spy and a US citizen, who was subsequently identified as Jensen Huang through a process known as "unmasking".
 Alice Huang has not responded to the paper's requests for comment.
 She is linked to Singapore-based data centre firm Megaspeed. The firm told the NYT last month its current leadership took the allegations seriously and had appointed external legal advisers to conduct an internal investigation.

 Jensen Huang is a 'fine person' who has done 'incredible job', says Trump published at 02:07 GMT 02:07 GMT 
 Media caption, Watch: Trump speaks to reporters after Nvidia investigation announced
 US President Donald Trump says he has not spoken to the Nvidia boss since news of the investigation emerged.
 "I just know he's a fine person, but you never know what's going on," Trump told reporters late on Sunday, adding that he had "done an amazing job for our country".
 The New York Times reported in late October that Trump had been briefed last year on intelligence alleging Alice Huang was spying on China's behalf.
 Asked by reporters whether he now wished he had "acted on the intelligence" at the time, Trump responded: "No, I don't think so. I think he's an honourable guy."
 China has previously rejected allegations of an espionage operation targeting the Nvidia chief, describing the claims as "groundless speculation" .

 Tech world stunned by extraordinary news of Nvidia investigation published at 01:57 GMT 01:57 GMT 
 Zoe Kleinman 
Technology and AI editor 
 My phone is blowing up tonight with messages from tech sector contacts who are stunned by this extraordinary news.
 Nvidia is one of the world's biggest and most successful tech companies, and Jensen Huang has run it for over three decades.
 He has rescued the firm from almost going broke more than once, and took a punt on AI a long time before the rest of the world did.
 His decision to make Nvidia chips - originally designed for gaming - the best in the business for AI development has now paid off in spades, and the company is worth trillions.
 This is a big blow for a man who is renowned for being a workaholic, a perfectionist and someone who expects incredibly high standards from his staff.
 He has fallen spectacularly short of his own values and in an embarrassingly old-fashioned way. There was no sophisticated AI-enabled sting at play here, he simply followed his heart.
 At the moment, the Nvidia board says Huang is committed to carrying on the company's leadership. 
 But it remains to be seen whether the staff from whom he expects so much decide to tolerate his flaws now, especially given the enormous potential consequences of them.

 What has Nvidia said about the investigation? published at 01:47 GMT 01:47 GMT 
 A statement issued by Nvidia's board of directors said it would begin an investigation in "light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort".
 It continued: "The Board prioritises US national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of Nvidia and its shareholders.
 "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information.
 "Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it."

 'There is no excuse' says Huang as he admits being 'unfaithful' to his wife published at 01:27 GMT 01:27 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Jensen Huang admitted to having been "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children, in a statement shared with Nvidia staff on Sunday.
 "There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."
 Addressing his colleagues and staff, he said: "My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility."
 His statement continued: "Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, Nvidia's Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully.
 "I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American."

 Who is Jensen Huang? published at 01:16 GMT 01:16 GMT 
 Nvidia is one of the world's largest companies and seen as central to making the hardware for emerging AI technologies. Jensen Huang has been in charge of it for more than 30 years.
 Huang was born in Taiwan and was nine years old when his family moved to the West Coast in the US.
 He graduated as an electrical engineer from Oregon State University, and then with a masters degree in the same field from Stanford University.
 He married his college sweetheart and lab partner, Lori Mills, also an electrical engineer. The couple have two children.
 Huang worked at US chip firm AMD before co-founding Nvidia in 1993. 
 The company was originally known for chips that process graphics, particularly for computer games. Eventually it changed its focus to AI, a field it now dominates.
 Huang has rescued the firm from almost going broke on more than one occasion. The microchip manufacturer is now worth some $4.5 trillion, making it one of the most valuable companies ever. 
 It is a central player in AI infrastructure, providing chips to leading developers including OpenAI and Meta.

 Nvidia launches investigation into CEO's affair with suspected Chinese spy published at 01:14 GMT 01:14 GMT 
 US tech giant Nvidia has opened an independent investigation following reports its CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.
 The company, one of the most valuable in the world, said its board had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised, adding that the CEO was committed to continuing to lead the company.
 Separately, Jensen Huang admitted to having been "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children.
 US intelligence officials believed that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who had a close relationship with Jensen Huang, was a spy for Beijing, according to a New York Times report , external .
 Jensen Huang said he took "full responsibility" for what he did, adding that he had fallen short of his responsibilities to Nvidia's employees, board and shareholders.
